title: Auto-release a publish hold when the push provably did not land: a definite push failure plus an unchanged remote tip
description:
LEAN FIRST SLICE of task-21be6e9055984413a651ce6ee331e2c8 ("An UNKNOWN publish effect has no operator exit"), filed by architect-73d103f8 on 2026-09-18. The owner chose this ordering: this AUTOMATIC resolve lands first as one row; task-21be6e90's explicit OPERATOR command (a new command kind, which this epic's own rail makes a four-row job) stays queued and declares dependsOn on this row. This row adds NO command kind.

THE DEFECT (source reads at HEAD). apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-publisher.ts: `if (!observed.ok || observed.sha !== candidate.approval.sha) return unknown();` (:67). A push the remote REFUSED (ssh key missing, non-fast-forward, protected branch, 403) never moves the remote to the approved sha, so every pass is UNKNOWN forever. The only release from phase PUBLISHING is reason "PUBLISHED" (:74; repository-execution-port.ts:16 `PUBLISHING: ["PUBLISHING","BLOCKED"]` and :102). So the reservation holds PUBLISHING for ever, every node.deliver is REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_BUSY, and the whole product stalls on one refused push.

WHY THE DAEMON CANNOT RESOLVE IT TODAY: IT KEEPS NO EVIDENCE. The intent (`moe-publication-intent/1`, publication-effect-ledger.ts) records the candidate, owner digest, reservation revision and controller, but NOT the remote tip before the push and NOT the push's outcome. The push result is DISCARDED: `try { await config.git.push(candidate); } catch { /* reconcile below */ }` (:62-65) ignores even a clean `{ ok: false }` from the port. So nothing distinguishes "never landed" from "landed and later moved".

THE RULE THIS ROW IMPLEMENTS — BOTH CONDITIONS, NEVER ONE. A publish is resolved NOT_TRANSMITTED automatically only when (1) the push DEFINITELY FAILED — the port returned a clean refusal for a non-zero git exit, not a throw and not a result lost across a crash — AND (2) the remote tip observed AFTER equals the tip observed BEFORE the push. Condition (1) alone is not enough: git can exit non-zero after the remote ref already moved (a failing post-receive hook). Condition (2) alone is not enough: a push that SUCCEEDED and was then force-pushed back by someone else also leaves the tip unchanged, and resolving that would permit a SECOND transmission — breaking the single-transmission invariant node-publisher.ts states at :26 (\"A persisted effect intent is never permission to repeat a push. Recovery only observes.\"). A successful push is therefore NEVER auto-resolved, and an indeterminate one falls to task-21be6e90's operator exit.

SCOPE LIMIT, STATED TO THE OWNER BEFORE THEY CHOSE: this fixes FUTURE refused pushes only. A publish ALREADY stuck has no recorded pre-push tip or push outcome, so it cannot be proven untransmitted and stays UNKNOWN until task-21be6e90's operator command lands.

HAZARD — do not widen the intent. Record the pre-push tip and the push outcome as a SEPARATE, ADDITIVE event on the intent's aggregate, not as new keys on `moe-publication-intent/1`. Widening an exact-key-set durable record without a legacy path is the failure fixed three times on this board today (task-2bb0bc24 governance ledger; the RepositoryRemoteBound hazard in task-baefab32).

node-publisher.ts IS EDITED BY THREE ROWS: this one, task-baefab32 and task-04160615. This row is the most urgent (a stalled live product), so it goes FIRST and task-baefab32 declares dependsOn on it; in the shared checkout a whole-file pathspec commit sweeps a peer's uncommitted hunk.
definitionOfDone: A refused push (the port returns a clean non-zero-exit refusal) whose remote tip is unchanged from the recorded pre-push tip is resolved automatically: a REFUSED receipt with code PUBLISH_NOT_LANDED carrying both tips is recorded, the reservation is released from PUBLISHING with the new reason PUBLISH_NOT_TRANSMITTED, and a fresh publish decision can push again. Asserted by value on the receipt, the reservation phase and the release reason.

Each half of the rule is necessary, one arm each, each asserting the publish stays UNKNOWN and the reservation stays PUBLISHING: a clean push failure whose remote tip MOVED; a SUCCESSFUL push whose tip was then reset to the pre-push value (the force-push-back race); a push whose outcome is indeterminate (the port threw, or the transmission record is absent); and an unreadable pre-push tip. The single-transmission invariant arms in node-publisher-approved.test.ts pass UNCHANGED.

PUBLISH_NOT_TRANSMITTED is accepted only from phase PUBLISHING: a repository-execution-port.test.ts arm asserts the exact refusal REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_TRANSITION_INVALID (or the port's measured code) from every other phase.

The pre-push tip and push outcome are recorded as an ADDITIVE event; `moe-publication-intent/1`'s shape is unchanged, and an intent recorded before this row (no transmission event) still decodes and is left UNKNOWN rather than auto-resolved.

A live-shaped arm on a real bare remote that REFUSES the push (e.g. a pre-receive hook that exits 1) drives publish -> refused -> auto-resolved -> a fresh publish that pushes exactly once; plus apps/daemon/CLAUDE.md's publisher bullet states the rule. Gates quoted with `Test Files N passed` lines for src/orchestrator/node-publisher* and src/repository/**, and `pnpm typecheck`.

implementationPlan.description: Wire the rule into the publisher. In apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-publisher.ts, ONLY on a fresh intent: observe the remote tip BEFORE pushing (a sha, null when the branch is absent, or UNREADABLE when observe refuses); stop discarding the push result and classify it ACCEPTED / REJECTED / INDETERMINATE from step 2's codes — a throw is INDETERMINATE; record ONE transmission event holding both, immediately after the push returns. Then, after the existing post-push observe, keep the success path at :67-74 exactly as it is. Add ONE branch before `return unknown()`: when the transmission record exists AND its outcome is REJECTED AND its pre-push tip is a KNOWN value AND the post-push observe succeeded AND the observed tip EQUALS the pre-push tip, record a REFUSED receipt for THIS decisionId with code `PUBLISH_NOT_LANDED` and a detail naming the branch and the unchanged tip, then release the reservation with `"PUBLISH_NOT_TRANSMITTED"`, and report it. Write the both-conditions rule as a comment at the site with one line per condition on why it alone is insufficient. A replayed intent never pushes and never records a transmission: recovery only observes, and a crash between push and record leaves NO record, so that publish stays UNKNOWN — correct, and forward-compatible with task-21be6e90's operator exit. The file must stay under 250 lines.
implementationPlan.note:
node-publisher.ts is 145 lines; publish() is 49 lines.
(1) `transmit(request, candidate)` runs ONLY when `fresh`. It observes the tip BEFORE the push: sha, null when absent, or PUBLICATION_TIP_UNREADABLE when observe refuses OR throws. Then it pushes and KEEPS the result: ok -> ACCEPTED, code === PUBLISH_PUSH_REJECTED (imported from git-publication-port, the single source of the literal) -> REJECTED, and any other refusal or a throw -> INDETERMINATE. Right after the push it records ONE recordPublicationTransmission. If the record write throws, the outer catch answers UNKNOWN, no record exists, and the next pass stays UNKNOWN unless the remote holds the sha.
(2) The success path (observe, then the PUSHED receipt, then release PUBLISHED) is byte-identical except its guard line. `if (!observed.ok || observed.sha !== approval.sha) return unknown();` became a block returning `(observed.ok ? notLanded(...) : null) ?? unknown()`.
(3) notLanded(): the transmission record must exist AND have outcome REJECTED AND tipBefore !== UNREADABLE AND tipBefore === the observed tip (both string|null, UNREADABLE excluded first). The post-push observe must have succeeded (the caller passes only observed.ok). It then records a REFUSED receipt for THIS decisionId: code PUBLISH_NOT_LANDED, branch/sha = the approved candidate, url null, and a detail naming the sha, the branch and BOTH tips ("the remote tip was <X|absent> before the push and is <Y|absent> after it"). It requires the persisted receipt's refusal code to be PUBLISH_NOT_LANDED, which guards against replaying some other receipt. Only then does giveBack() release with "PUBLISH_NOT_TRANSMITTED" and report {outcome:"REFUSED", detail:"PUBLISH_NOT_LANDED: …"}. Any miss answers UNKNOWN. The both-conditions rule is a comment at the site, with one line per condition on why it is insufficient alone.
(4) CRASH WINDOW, closed. It is written receipt-first: releasing first would, on a crash, let the next pass acquire a NEW RESERVED hold whose ownerDigest mismatches the intent, a permanent stall. publishOnce now re-drives a decision whose receipt is PUBLISH_NOT_LANDED while its hold is still publish:<decisionId>, the same shape as the existing PUSHED crash path. publish(request, settled) then gives the PUBLISHING hold back WITHOUT re-reading the remote: the receipt is the decision, so a later foreign push cannot strand the hold.
(5) A replayed intent (fresh=false) never pushes and never records a transmission. A crash between push and record leaves NO record, so that publish stays UNKNOWN (the operator exit, task-21be6e90).

Filed by me this session as the lean first slice of task-21be6e90; the owner chose to land it FIRST, with task-21be6e90's operator command queued behind it (dependsOn set). Re-measured at HEAD 2026-09-18 — source reads unless marked.

(1) THE STUCK PATH. apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-publisher.ts (100 lines): a fresh intent pushes inside `try { await config.git.push(candidate); } catch { /* reconcile below */ }` (:62-65), DISCARDING the port's return value; then `if (!observed.ok || observed.sha !== candidate.approval.sha) return unknown();` (:67). A refused push never reaches the approved sha, so it is UNKNOWN every pass. The only release from PUBLISHING is `"PUBLISHED"` (:74). Line anchors in the parent row's reopen reason (:98-101, :124) are STALE — the file is 100 lines.

(2) THE DISTINCTION ALREADY EXISTS AND IS THROWN AWAY. apps/daemon/src/repository/git-publication-port.ts:19-21, the git runner: `code: error === null ? 0 : typeof error.code === "number" ? error.code : null`. So git that RAN and exited non-zero yields a NUMBER; a timeout, a kill or a spawn failure (error.code a string like ENOENT, or absent) yields NULL. `push` then collapses both into `publicationRefused("PUBLISH_PUSH_UNKNOWN")` (:66-67), and a throw in the outer catch does the same. Splitting that one return is the whole enabling change.

(3) THE REFUSAL CODE IS FREE-FORM, AND push HAS ONE CONSUMER. `export const publicationRefused = (code: string): PublicationRefusal => ...` (publication-approval-contracts.ts:21) takes a plain string: there is no closed code roster to update. `git grep -n "git.push("` finds exactly ONE caller, node-publisher.ts:64 (the other `.push(` hits are Array.push).

(4) THE RESERVATION MACHINE. `RepositoryExecutionReleaseReason` is a string union in apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-execution-contracts.ts:10. The port's release guard is a ternary chain at repository-execution-port.ts:101-105 mapping each reason to the ONE prior phase it may leave; a reason missing from the chain falls through to `false` — it fails CLOSED. `PUBLISHING: ["PUBLISHING", "BLOCKED"]` at :16 is the TRANSITION map (phase to phase); release is separate and keyed on reason.

(5) THE CARD ALREADY UN-STICKS ON A RECEIPT — measured, because it looked like a gap. apps/daemon/src/http/run-goal-publication.ts decides UNKNOWN only for a request with NO receipt: `if (state.receipts.has(pending.decisionId)) continue;` precedes the intent check. The intent is append-only and survives, but once a REFUSED receipt exists for the SAME decisionId, that decision is skipped, and the card reports outcome REFUSED with the receipt's code instead of UNKNOWN — which re-enables Publish. So recording the receipt for the right decisionId is what frees the card; run-goal-publication.ts needs NO edit.

(6) THE INTENT MUST NOT BE WIDENED. It is `moe-publication-intent/1` in apps/daemon/src/repository/publication-effect-ledger.ts (VERSION at :10, reader at :24). The pre-push tip and the push outcome go in a SEPARATE, ADDITIVE event on the intent's aggregate. Widening an exact-key-set durable record without a legacy path is the failure fixed three times on this board today.

(7) THE PATH CAP. The event's TYPE is declared in publication-effect-ledger.ts beside its writer and reader, not in publication-effect-contracts.ts, to hold the row at exactly 10 files. node-publisher-approved.test.ts is deliberately NOT an owned path: DoD 2 requires its single-transmission arms to pass UNCHANGED.
